claims.text: Uniaxial tensile tests coupled with digital image correlation can effectively characterize the mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Variations in strain rate produce measurable differences in the yield strength of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Variations in strain rate produce measurable differences in the ductility of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
As-cast or homogenized FeNiCrMn samples have an initially uniform microstructure.
DIC can monitor surface-strain evolution during controlled-rate uniaxial tensile loading.
Grain boundaries and dislocation structures mediate the initiation and propagation of strain localization in FeNiCrMn alloy.
Tensile stress drives dislocation motion and interaction in FeNiCrMn alloy.
Dislocation interactions and grain-boundary effects generate strain-localization patterns that vary with strain rate.
Strain-rate-dependent localization affects the yield strength of FeNiCrMn alloy.
Strain-rate-dependent localization affects the ductility of FeNiCrMn alloy.
At lower strain rates, FeNiCrMn alloy exhibits a more uniform strain distribution.
The more uniform strain distribution predicted at lower strain rates leads to higher ductility.
At higher strain rates, FeNiCrMn alloy exhibits greater strain localization.
The strain localization predicted at higher strain rates increases yield strength.
The strain localization predicted at higher strain rates reduces ductility.
DIC provides spatiotemporal strain resolution that standard uniaxial tensile-test data lack.
Significant phase separation may cause mechanical responses different from those predicted for uniform as-cast or homogenized FeNiCrMn samples.
Additional alloying elements may cause mechanical responses different from those of the stated FeNiCrMn system.
